check their proxy lists purchased for use with Telegram Expert to ensure their status is fine and that they are displayed correctly in the program. All added proxies will be shown in a table. Table Overview The table displays the following data: host – the proxy server address (IP or domain). port – the port used for connection. login – the username for proxy authentication. password – the password for accessing the proxy. type – the proxy type (HTTP, SOCKS5). version – the proxy protocol version (e.g., ipv4). response – the proxy response speed. status – the result of the proxy validation (ok — the proxy is live, bad — the proxy could not connect during validation). actions – available actions for the proxy (validation, deletion). The software only works with ipv4 proxies. The table is easy to manage — users can select proxies to validate or delete them entirely from the list. If bad proxies are identified during validation, they can also be removed with the click of a button. Important Notes If you are confident that your proxies are functional, it is recommended to test them not only using the proxy validation module but also by conducting a standard account ban check using these proxies. Sometimes, the proxy pool checker may report a connection error and mark proxies as non-functional (bad), even if they are actually working. During proxy validation, a high ping (response time) may occur in certain geographical regions. In such cases, it is recommended to increase the response time threshold to 45 seconds and set up 15 retry attempts for proxy switching. This can result in proxies initially marked as non-functional (red) being marked as functional (green). However, high-quality proxies should consistently deliver stable results. Adding New Proxies New proxies can be added to the list below. The user needs to select the protocol and then provide the required details in the format ip:port:login:pass . After entering the data, click the «Add Proxy» button — if the data is correct, it will appear in the list.
